accepted.s: The burden of proving that an activity is benign, in the context of the precautionary principle, rests upon:
o: The person or entity undertaking the activity
accepted.x: Under the precautionary principle, the burden of proof shifts to the actor undertaking the potentially harmful activity to demonstrate that it is benign.
accepted.tq: Apply the principle by identifying who must establish that the risky activity is harmless.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the scope of the Polluter Pays Principle?
o: Payment of a fixed penalty without restoration of the affected environment
Transfer of all environmental liabilities to the State
Bearing the costs of remediation as well as compensation for the damage caused
Payment only for the private compensation claimed by victims
accepted.x: The Polluter Pays Principle includes both remediation of the environmental damage and compensation for the affected persons or resources.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the complete legal consequence from the narrower idea of merely paying a fine.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
a. Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
b. Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
c. M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
 d. M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath

List-II (Subject or principle)
i. Public trust doctrine
 ii. Oleum gas leak and absolute liability
 iii. Tanneries polluting the Palar River
 iv. Chemical units in Bichhri required to pay for clean-up

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Vellore concerned Palar River pollution by tanneries and applied precautionary and polluter pays principles; Bichhri concerned chemical-unit clean-up; Oleum gas leak established absolute liability; Kamal Nath applied public trust doctrine.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure case-fact pair and eliminate codes with swapped cases.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s:
With reference to the Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum case, consider the following statements:
1. It concerned pollution of the Palar River by tanneries.
2. It applied both the precautionary principle and the Polluter Pays Principle.
3. It concerned the diversion of forest land without Central approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Vellore case concerned tannery pollution of the Palar River and applied both principles. Diversion of forest land is associated with the Forest (Conservation) Act, not this case.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated case-fact statement among closely connected environmental principles.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: The principle of absolute liability, under which a hazardous industry is liable without exceptions, was laid down in connection with:
o: Pollution of the Palar River by tanneries
accepted.x: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987), arising from the Oleum gas leak, established absolute liability for hazardous industries without exceptions.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive industrial accident with the legal principle it produced.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: T.N. Godavarman case — any area recorded as forest
Taj Trapezium case — chemical units in Rajasthan required to pay for clean-up
Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar — pollution-free water and air under Article 21
M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath — State holds natural resources in trust for the public
accepted.x: The Bichhri case of Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action concerned chemical units in Rajasthan and clean-up costs. The Taj Trapezium case mandated the use of CNG.
accepted.tq: Check the case-specific subject rather than matching merely by environmental theme.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: The decision that recognised pollution-free water and air as part of the right under Article 21 was given in:
o: T.N. Godavarman v. Union of India
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India
Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
accepted.x: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar (1991) recognised the right to pollution-free water and air under Article 21.
accepted.tq: Use the Article 21 association to distinguish the case from other environmental precedents.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: Which environmental case is associated with the mandating of CNG?
accepted.x: The Taj Trapezium case (1997) mandated the use of CNG as an environmental protection measure.
accepted.tq: Identify the unusual remedy associated with the correct case.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: The T.N. Godavarman case is significant because its forest-related protection covers:
o: Only forests located within protected areas
Only reserved forests notified under the Wildlife Act
accepted.x: The T.N. Godavarman case (1995) covers any area recorded as forest, rather than only formally notified reserved forests.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of the category by focusing on the word ‘any’.
accepted.sec: Environmental principles - precautionary, polluter pays, public trust, absolute liability (and the cases)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 — protection of wildlife and habitats and regulation of hunting
Water Act, 1974 — control of air pollution only
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the Pollution Control Boards
accepted.x: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects wildlife and habitats and regulates hunting. The other purposes are associated with different laws.
accepted.tq: Match each Act with its core purpose and reject neighbouring environmental subjects.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1974 and created the pollution control boards.
accepted.tq: Separate the closely spaced years of the principal environmental Acts.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: The Central Pollution Control Board is best described as:
o: A constitutional body created under the Environment Protection Act
A judicial body constituted under Article 21
A statutory body under the Water Act, also functioning under the Air Act, 1981
A temporary body established under the EIA Notification, 2006
accepted.x: The CPCB was established in 1974 as a statutory body under the Water Act and also operates under the Air Act, 1981. It sets standards and monitors air and water.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct parent statute and distinguish a statutory body from constitutional and temporary bodies.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior Central approval for diversion of forest land.
2. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1981.
3. The Air Act was amended in 1987 to introduce stricter penalties.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Forest Act requires prior Central approval for diversion, while the Air Act dates from 1981 and was amended in 1987 with stricter penalties.
accepted.tq: Verify each year and the associated legal consequence before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — legal basis for EIA and CRZ notifications
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — creation of the pollution control boards
accepted.x: The pollution control boards were created under the Water Act, 1974. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella law whose Section 3 supports EIA and CRZ notifications.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that assigns a body’s origin to the wrong statute.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: The Ganga Action Plan began in:
accepted.x: The Ganga Action Plan began in 1986; 1982 is the incorrect year associated with it.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the stated year and the close but incorrect alternative.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: Under the Water Act and the Air Act, the respective provisions under which State Pollution Control Boards can levy compensation are:
accepted.x: SPCBs can levy compensation under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act.
accepted.tq: Keep the two similar statutory section numbers in their correct Act-wise order.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: Under the Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026, the Fund is constituted under which provision, and how is it divided between the States/Union Territories and the Centre?
o: Section 33A of the Water Act; 75% and 25%
Section 31A of the Air Act; 25% and 75%
accepted.x: The Environmental Protection Fund Rules, 2026 place the Fund under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act. Seventy-five per cent goes to States/UTs and 25 per cent to the Centre.
accepted.tq: Combine the enabling provision with the percentage split instead of treating them as separate figures.
accepted.sec: Environmental Acts and bodies - year and purpose

accepted.s: The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in:
accepted.x: The Eco-Mark scheme was launched in 1991 to label environment-friendly consumer products.
accepted.tq: Use the chronology of environmental initiatives to distinguish the scheme’s launch year.
accepted.sec: Eco-Mark scheme - launch, what it certifies, products, administering bodies

accepted.s: Which symbol is used as the logo of the Eco-Mark scheme?
accepted.x: The Eco-Mark logo is an earthen pot, used for labelling environment-friendly consumer products.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive logo rather than the general environmental purpose of the scheme.
accepted.sec: Eco-Mark scheme - launch, what it certifies, products, administering bodies

accepted.s: Which institution certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme?
accepted.x: The Bureau of Indian Standards certifies products under the Eco-Mark scheme.
accepted.tq: Identify the administering certification institution and avoid confusing it with an environmental regulator.
accepted.sec: Eco-Mark scheme - launch, what it certifies, products, administering bodies

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT covered among the products notified under the Eco-Mark scheme?
accepted.x: The notified product groups include soaps and detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics, aerosols and food items. Drugs and antibiotics are not covered.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded product from a list containing several covered categories.
accepted.sec: Eco-Mark scheme - launch, what it certifies, products, administering bodies

accepted.s: The National Environment Policy was adopted in:
accepted.x: The National Environment Policy was adopted in 2006 and serves as India’s overarching environment policy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the policy year from the years of the umbrella Act and Eco-Mark scheme.
accepted.sec: National Environment Policy - year, objectives, principles

accepted.s: The central idea of the National Environment Policy, 2006 is that:
o: Economic growth must always be stopped to protect natural resources
Conservation and livelihood security are mutually exclusive
Environmental protection should be separated from development planning
Conservation and livelihood security can proceed together
accepted.x: The NEP 2006 rests on the idea that conservation and livelihood security go together rather than being opposed to each other.
accepted.tq: Apply the policy’s balancing approach instead of choosing an extreme conservation-versus-development position.
accepted.sec: National Environment Policy - year, objectives, principles

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the National Environment Policy, 2006?
o: Elimination of all development activity in ecologically sensitive areas
Integration of environmental concerns into development plans
accepted.x: The NEP objectives include conservation of critical resources, inter-generational equity and integration of environment into development plans. It does not prescribe elimination of all development activity.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme statement that goes beyond the policy’s balanced objectives.
accepted.sec: National Environment Policy - year, objectives, principles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Environment Policy, 2006:
1. It seeks efficient use of environmental resources.
2. It includes good environmental governance as an objective.
3. It recognises livelihood security for poor tribal communities.
4. It includes the precautionary approach, Polluter Pays Principle and public trust doctrine among its principles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the objectives and principles of the National Environment Policy, 2006.
accepted.tq: Check whether each listed objective or principle belongs to the same policy framework before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: National Environment Policy - year, objectives, principles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of EIA in India:
1. The EIA Notification, 1994 was issued on 27 January 1994 under the Environment (Protection) Act.
2. Before the 1994 notification, environmental clearance was only an administrative decision.
3. The EIA Notification, 2006 replaced the 1994 notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 1994 notification was issued on 27 January under the EPA, clearance had earlier been only administrative, and the 2006 notification replaced it.
accepted.tq: Arrange the legal transition in sequence and verify both the date and the status of clearance before 1994.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 introduced which major change in the basis for appraisal?
o: A shift from investment size to impact potential
A shift from public consultation to administrative approval only
A shift from project categories to product certification
A shift from impact potential to investment size
accepted.x: The 2006 notification shifted the test from investment size to impact potential and made clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
accepted.tq: Focus on the reversed comparison between the old and new bases of appraisal.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, environmental clearance became compulsory for how many project categories?
accepted.x: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.
accepted.tq: Test the precise statutory count rather than the broader idea of compulsory clearance.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Category)
a. Category A
b. Category B
c. Category A clearance
 d. Category B clearance

List-II (Authority)
i. State Environment Impact Assessment Authority
 ii. State Expert Appraisal Committee
 iii. Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre
 iv. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC. Category B projects are appraised by the State EAC and cleared by SEIAA.
accepted.tq: Separate the appraisal authority from the clearance authority before matching the categories.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of stages in the EIA process?
accepted.x: The stages are Screening, Scoping, Public consultation and Appraisal. Screening applies only to Category B projects.
accepted.tq: Use the process sequence and place the decision-oriented appraisal stage last.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s:
With reference to EIA stages, consider the following statements:
1. Screening is applicable only to Category B projects.
2. Defence and strategic projects are exempt from public consultation.
3. Scoping precedes public consultation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Screening is limited to Category B projects, the specified defence and strategic projects are exempt from public consultation, and scoping comes before public consultation.
accepted.tq: Check the exception and the process order together rather than treating every EIA stage as universal.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: Which of the following was proposed by the Draft EIA 2020 notification?
o: Abolition of environmental clearance for Category A projects
Post-facto clearance on payment of penalties and a shorter public consultation period
Removal of all public consultation requirements
Replacement of impact potential by investment size
accepted.x: The Draft EIA 2020 proposed post-facto clearance upon payment of penalties and a shorter public consultation period. It attracted widespread protest and was not finalised.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact controversial proposals without extending them into absolute claims.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding post-facto environmental clearance is correct?
o: Vanashakti v. Union of India struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum allowing ex post facto clearances.
The S.P. Muthuraman case held retrospective environmental clearances legal.
Vanashakti v. Union of India upheld the 2021 Office Memorandum allowing ex post facto clearances.
Both cases made post-facto clearance compulsory for Category B projects.
accepted.x: In Vanashakti v. Union of India, the Supreme Court struck down the 2021 Office Memorandum permitting ex post facto clearances. The S.P. Muthuraman case also held retrospective environmental clearances illegal.
accepted.tq: Use the legal outcome trap by distinguishing ‘struck down’ and ‘upheld’ and checking the case names.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: The ruling in Vanashakti v. Union of India regarding ex post facto clearances applies:
o: Only to projects in forest areas
Retrospectively to every project approved since 1994
accepted.x: The Supreme Court’s ruling striking down the 2021 Office Memorandum applies prospectively.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the legal effects of prospective and retrospective operation.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: In the event of the lapse of a State’s SEIAA or SEAC, which bodies step in as backup bodies under the July 2026 arrangement?
accepted.x: The backup bodies are SAEIA and SCEIA, which step in when a State’s SEIAA or SEAC lapses.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the specially named backup bodies from the regular central and State authorities.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft

accepted.s: What change was made in July 2026 concerning the tenure of members of the relevant EIA bodies?
o: It was increased from two years to five years
It was reduced from four years to two years
It was increased from three years to four years
accepted.x: The member tenure was increased from three years to four years under the July 2026 arrangement.
accepted.tq: Compare the two close tenure figures and reject unsupported extreme durations.
accepted.sec: EIA - notifications, categories A/B, stages, EIA 2020 draft
